guide.summary: Toronto's towers, museums, markets and parks, with brunch spots, dinners, cocktail bars, bakeries and cafés checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Plan around Monday closures: St. Lawrence Market's South Market and the Aga Khan Museum are closed Mondays, while the Gardiner Museum stays open until 9pm on Wednesdays.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: St. Lawrence Market's South Market and the Aga Khan Museum close on Mondays, and Canoe is closed to the public on Saturdays and Sundays. Maha's is closed Wednesdays and national holidays.

toolkit.label: Free entry
toolkit.copy: The Bata Shoe Museum is free every Sunday, the Aga Khan Museum is free on Wednesdays from 4 to 8pm, and the Gardiner Museum is free after 4pm on Wednesdays.

toolkit.label: Booking
toolkit.copy: Pai's downtown reservations open 30 days in advance and aren't taken by phone. Canoe takes online reservations up to 3 months ahead for parties of up to 12.

toolkit.label: Walk-ins
toolkit.copy: Bar Raval states "NO RESERVATIONS" and Maha's is walk-in only. Simpl Things takes online bookings for up to 6 but says walk-ins are always accepted.

guide.dek: Pair a downtown landmark with a museum each day, and book dinners ahead while saving bars and brunch for walk-ins.
intro: Toronto's core sights cluster near the waterfront. The CN Tower, at 290 Bremner Blvd., sells timed tickets online, including EdgeWalk and reservations at its 360 Restaurant, and it is hosting a Toronto Biennial of Art work until December 20, 2026. Ripley's Aquarium of Canada sits next door at 288 Bremner Boulevard, and Steam Whistle Brewing at 255 Bremner Blvd. takes tour bookings. East of downtown, St. Lawrence Market's South Market opens Tuesday to Sunday and closes Mondays, with the Saturday Farmer's Market starting at 5am.

For museums, the Royal Ontario Museum at 100 Queen's Park runs Psychedelics until December 6, 2026, and opens until 8:30pm on the third Tuesday of the month. Across the road, the Gardiner Museum stays open until 9pm on Wednesdays, with free entry after 4pm. The Bata Shoe Museum on Bloor Street West is free every Sunday and opened its beaded-footwear exhibition, Brilliant, on October 22. Further north, the Aga Khan Museum shows Saks Afridi: SpaceMosque until March 7, 2027, and closes on Mondays.

If you want a slower day, the Distillery Historic District at 55 Mill Street is open 364 days a year, and its Winter Village opens on November 12, 2026, with free entry Monday to Wednesday through December 13 and tickets on weekend evenings. Casa Loma opens daily from 9:30am to 5pm with date-specific tickets. High Park is a free outdoor option, but the City says its Animal Display is closed until Spring 2027. The Toronto Zoo opens daily from 9:30am to 4:30pm, with last admission an hour before closing.

For food, book dinner ahead. Pai's downtown reservations open 30 days in advance, Canoe on the 54th floor of the TD Bank Tower takes bookings up to three months ahead and is closed on weekends, and Alo serves from Tuesday to Saturday. For breakfast, Maha's on Greenwood Avenue is walk-in only and closed Wednesdays, and Lady Marmalade on Broadview opens daily from 8:30 to 3. In the evening, Bar Raval on College Street takes no reservations and opens daily from 1pm to 1am.
summaryCards: Start with the CN Tower and Ripley's Aquarium on Bremner Boulevard, then walk to St. Lawrence Market, remembering it's closed on Mondays.
Have a walk-in brunch at Maha's (closed Wednesdays) or Lady Marmalade, then visit the Gardiner or Bata Shoe Museum on Bloor and Queen's Park.
Pai's downtown tables open 30 days ahead and Canoe's three months ahead, while Bar Raval and Maha's take no reservations.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several sites could not be read: the Art Gallery of Ontario (HTTP 403), Pilot Coffee and Balzac's (HTTP 429), Mildred's Temple Kitchen (connection refused), Sisters & Co., Roselle, Bar Pompette and Bakerbots (domain not found), Nord Lyon (SSL error), and Mother (no readable content). These failures are not evidence of closure. The Hockey Hall of Fame and Toronto Botanical Garden were left out because no street address loaded, and Toronto Island was left out because the City pages read gave no terminal address. Some confirmed places are only partly published: the CN Tower's weekly hours and the opening hours for Steam Whistle Brewing, Harbord Bakery and High Park were not shown, Ripley's showed only the current day's hours, Alo's closing time is not given, and several restaurants, bars and cafés have no 2026-dated content beyond a footer or published hours (medium confidence).
